status: Newly discovered candidates for editorial selection; original weekly eight retained. Visuals are proposed, not implemented.

papers.title: BoundedGS: the memory peak depends on what stays alive together.
papers.full_title: BoundedGS: Memory-Efficient High-Resolution Training for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.change: New to coverage via the October 27 arXiv listing, but submitted October 25 before the previous cutoff. Official implementation is present; initial commit October 25 at 11:13:06 UTC. A link-only commit October 27 is not a new algorithm release.
papers.summary: Completes local rasterization/backward work and frees those caches before processing another region. Gradients accumulate across the full view, followed by one update. Adaptive regions, compact projection/gradients and bounded image supply control different memory peaks.
papers.evaluation: Authors train once per scene on 13 scenes using an RTX 4090 and a shared modified baseline. Five 5K outdoor scenes average 9.97→1.76 GiB temporary rendering working set; PSNR 24.44→24.42 and training 36.7→33.9 minutes. Fixed-model resolution sweeps are separate diagnostics.
papers.caveat: The 82.3% reduction is temporary rendering state, excluding model parameters, Adam state and persistent statistics—not total VRAM. CPU-assisted rebuilding raises host memory and costs time; no independent replication or broad GPU comparison.
papers.access: Official training/evaluation code and ablation configs verified. Authors tested Linux/RTX4090; Windows compilation/training is untested. Original BoundedGS code is MIT; inherited 3DGS/ImprovedGS components keep separate licenses. No installation or run.
papers.creator_implication: Potentially useful for high-resolution captured-scene training. This is reconstruction/rendering infrastructure, not generative 3D or a promise of 16K training in 1 GiB total memory.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed memory-lifetime lab: colored projection, raster, gradient and persistent-state blocks alongside image tiles. Change region budget/density/resolution; compare whole-frame versus sequential backward, accumulated gradients and one final update. Synthetic accounting, not measured BoundedGS.
papers.review_depth: Full paper methods/evaluation/accounting, official project and code/commit metadata; no execution.

papers.title: OmniShowcase: four photos still need a shared 3D story.
papers.full_title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
papers.change: Newly discovered in the October 27 listing; paper submission predates the October 26 cutoff. Official repository initial commit is October 27 at 10:42:26 UTC, but it contains README/assets and pending release checkboxes, not inference code.
papers.summary: Reconstructs geometry from reference views and supplies a surface-normal turntable as a video condition without requiring framewise alignment. Uses synthetic geometry-consistent camera trajectories and LoRA adaptation of Wan2.1-I2V-14B.
papers.evaluation: Authors compare four baselines using the same four references on 50 held-out ShowcaseBench subjects and 35 NAVI subjects. Held-out DINO: 0.799 versus 3DreamBooth 0.707; normalized/aligned geometry distance: 0.0824 versus 0.1717. Aesthetic score is lower, 0.574 versus 0.598.
papers.caveat: Selected subject-orbit evaluation is not general video SOTA. Masked metrics exclude backgrounds; geometry alignment normalizes scale. Synthetic backgrounds can look flat. References with changing poses fail under the static reconstruction condition; non-rigid subjects remain future work.
papers.access: Official project and repository verified; Showcase-4K, ShowcaseBench, inference, weights and training code all remain unchecked release items. No runnable release, checkpoint license or independent reproduction verified.
papers.creator_implication: Promising research for product turntables and orbit shots of rigid assets; it does not yet solve dynamic character identity or provide a ready-to-use tool.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed normal-map lab: orbit an asymmetric synthetic object, compare sparse RGB views with colored normals, expose unseen surfaces, and deliberately mismatch poses. Controls: reference count/angles, camera orbit, normal/RGB condition and pose disagreement. Analytic rendering, not model output.
papers.review_depth: Primary full paper including metrics/failure analysis and official project/repository release status; no execution.

visual_queue.title: The peak depends on which caches coexist.
visual_queue.idea: Image regions produce colored memory blocks, release their local caches and accumulate gradients before a single full-view update.
visual_queue.controls: Image resolution; Gaussian density; region budget; cache release order; persistent versus temporary memory; planned PNG/GIF.
visual_queue.misconception: An 82% temporary-memory reduction means 82% less total VRAM, or computing regions separately requires updating after every region.
visual_queue.connection: BoundedGS · 25 Oct paper, discovered 27 Oct. Proposed analytic memory-accounting lesson; not measured training.
visual_queue.recommendation: Strong next 3D mechanism graphic; prioritize temporary-versus-total memory and gradient accumulation.

visual_queue.title: Several views still need to agree on one shape.
visual_queue.idea: Reveal an asymmetric object through reference cameras and normal-map turntable, then show inconsistent poses breaking a shared static shape.
visual_queue.controls: Reference count/angles; orbit; normals/RGB; pose disagreement; unseen-surface overlay; planned PNG/GIF.
visual_queue.misconception: Adding reference images guarantees a shared 3D identity or resolves deformation across poses.
visual_queue.connection: OmniShowcase · 26 Oct paper, discovered 27 Oct. Synthetic projection/normal rendering, not inference.
visual_queue.recommendation: Useful orbit-shot explainer; label rigid-object scope prominently.
